memos.headline: AAPL and UNH Lead at 52-Week Highs; CAT and GOOGL Breaking Down Short-Term
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. AAPL is printing a fresh 52-week high with RSI at 71.6 and +19.8% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks — this is the strongest trend in the group, though the extended RSI and +10.3% premium to the 50-day mean warn of near-term pullback risk. UNH is similarly strong, sitting just 1.3% off its 52-week high with +17.6% 12-week relative strength and a more comfortable RSI of 57.9, making it my highest-conviction long. On the other side, CAT has dropped 7.6% in a week with RSI at 40.1 and -8.2% 4-week relative strength despite a massive 26-week gain — this looks like a momentum reversal and I'd avoid until it reclaims the 50-day mean (~928). GOOGL is also weakening with RSI at 42.2, -6.4% below its 50-day mean, and negative 4-week relative strength of -5.0%; a close below 335 would confirm a deeper correction.

views.note: At 52-week highs with dominant relative strength, but RSI 71.6 and +10.3% above 50d mean suggest chasing risk; would reassess below 310 (near 50d mean).
Near 52-week highs with +17.6% 12w relative strength and RSI 57.9 — best risk/reward long in the universe; invalidated below 400.
Only 1.7% off 52-week high, above both moving averages with positive relative strength and low ATR of 2.28%; would cut below 320.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Lead on Explosive Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between names delivering durable, accelerating earnings power and those showing margin erosion. NVDA's 2027Q1 quarter is extraordinary: $81.6B revenue (+85% YoY), $58.3B net income (+211% YoY), a 71.5% net margin, and only $8.5B total debt—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. GOOGL posted $110B revenue (+22% YoY) with net income surging 81% to $62.6B and a 57% net margin on just $14.8B debt, which is remarkable operating leverage. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin, and UNH grew revenue only 2% with flat net income and $77.9B in debt—both signal earnings fragility I'm unwilling to pay for. CAT surprised me positively with 22% revenue growth and 27% earnings growth at a 14.6% margin, though its $36.2B debt load relative to its income run-rate warrants monitoring.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, net margin 71.5%, net income +211% YoY on minimal $8.5B debt is the strongest earnings profile in the universe; a margin decline below 55% would change my view.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B with a 57% net margin and only $14.8B debt shows exceptional operating leverage; a deceleration in revenue growth below 10% would concern me.
Revenue +18% YoY, net income +23% YoY, 38.3% net margin, and manageable $40.3B debt demonstrate consistent durable earnings growth across cloud and enterprise segments.
Net income surged 77% YoY to $30.3B and margin expanded to 16.7%, but $122.6B total debt is the highest in the tech group and I need to see continued margin expansion to stay constructive.
Revenue +22% and earnings +27% YoY are strong, but $36.2B debt against ~$10B annualized earnings and cyclical exposure keep me neutral until I see sustained backlog data.
Revenue +17% and net income +19% YoY are solid but not exceptional relative to peers, and $82.7B total debt is elevated; I'd need accelerating services mix to get more constructive.
Revenue +10% and net income +12.6% YoY with a 33% margin are respectable for a bank, but the $449B debt stack and rate-cycle sensitivity limit my conviction.
Steady 7.4% revenue growth and 18.5% margin are defensive, but only 4.3% earnings growth suggests limited upside from here.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% margin with $33B debt signals severe earnings compression tied to commodity prices; I'd need margin recovery above 10% to reconsider.
Revenue grew only 2% YoY, net income was flat at $6.3B, and $77.9B debt is heavy—this is stagnating earnings power at an uncomfortable leverage level.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 3.5% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue for Caution on Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—the upper bound has been unchanged at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, and the June CPI print of 3.5% YoY gives the FOMC no room to ease further near-term. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.20%, down 10 bps over three months, which removes any urgency to cut. The 10-year yield has risen 29 bps over three months to 4.55% while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 13 bps to 0.41 pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and possibly some term premium rebuild. This backdrop favors short-duration, cash-flow-rich names and banks benefiting from a positively sloped curve, while it pressures high-multiple growth and rate-sensitive sectors. A CPI print falling below 3% or unemployment rising above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward imminent easing.

views.note: Positive yield curve (41 bps 10y-2y), stable labor market, and higher-for-longer rates support net interest margins for large banks.
Rising long-end yields and a Fed pause weigh on high-multiple growth names, though secular AI demand provides an offset I cannot size from macro data alone.
Duration headwind from 10y at 4.55% and sticky inflation limit multiple expansion, but strong cash generation provides a floor.
Similar duration sensitivity as AAPL; higher-for-longer rates cap upside on valuation multiples despite recurring revenue resilience.
Consumer spending resilience from low unemployment helps, but 3.5% CPI erodes real spending power and rising long rates pressure the multiple.
Staples benefit from pricing power in a 3.5% CPI environment and defensive positioning as the curve flattens and growth slows.
Stable macro backdrop is neither strongly positive nor negative for energy; no clear cyclical signal from current data.
Cyclical exposure is unattractive as the yield curve flattens and higher-for-longer rates dampen capex and construction activity.
Ad-driven revenue is tied to nominal GDP which benefits from 3.5% inflation, but rising discount rates limit multiple expansion.
Defensive healthcare with pricing power; benefits from a pause regime where investors rotate out of high-beta growth.

memos.headline: JPM and UNH Earnings Reactions Signal Positive Narrative Shifts; XOM and GOOGL Corporate Actions Warrant Monitoring
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K filing cadence and price reactions as my primary sentiment proxies this week, given the absence of GDELT tone data. JPM's Q2 earnings 8-K on 2026-07-14 drove a +2.5% price reaction, suggesting the market was positioned cautiously and the result surprised to the upside — a classic tone-turning-up-from-negative signal. UNH's earnings 8-K filed 2026-07-16 produced a +1.2% move, a more modest but still positive reaction that hints sentiment was not yet crowded bullish. GOOGL has had an unusually dense cluster of 8-Ks in early June — material agreements, bylaw amendments, and board changes — which could reflect either strategic repositioning or governance noise; I lack tone data to distinguish, so conviction is low. XOM's July 1 filing covering an acquisition completion, delisting notice, and bylaw amendments is the most complex single 8-K in the universe and deserves close attention for narrative development.

views.note: Earnings 8-K on 7/14 drove +2.5% price reaction, indicating sentiment was underweight and is now inflecting positively.
Earnings 8-K on 7/16 produced a +1.2% positive reaction, suggesting sentiment is turning but the move is modest enough that crowding risk is low.
Dense cluster of material agreement, governance, and board-change 8-Ks in early June creates ambiguity; without tone data I cannot separate strategic signal from noise.
July 1 8-K covering acquisition completion and delisting notice is complex and could shift narrative either way; staying neutral until tone clarifies.
New debt obligation filed 6/10 and two Other Events filings suggest active capital deployment, but no price reaction data to gauge market sentiment.
Board change on 7/2 and routine shareholder vote are low-signal events; no earnings catalyst or tone shift evident.
Single Reg FD disclosure on 7/14 provides minimal sentiment signal; awaiting earnings reaction for a directional view.
Only a board-level officer change 8-K on 6/5; insufficient information to form a sentiment view.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Still Elevated; Oil Decline Signals Demand or Supply Shift Worth Watching
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 42% over the past month to 283.91, yet remains 8% above its level three months ago, suggesting a structural overhang of policy risk even as acute fears recede. The VIX at 16.73 is benign and HY OAS at 2.71% is tightening on a 3-month basis (-15bp), so credit markets are not pricing imminent geopolitical disruption. WTI crude at $80.03 is down 17% over three months, which could reflect easing supply-chain or sanctions pressure on energy markets, or alternatively weakening global demand—either reading matters for the energy and industrial complex. Without explicit GDELT event data on new sanctions, export controls, or China policy actions in the evidence set, I have limited conviction on structural shifts and am relying on macro proxies and 8-K filings to infer the geopolitical backdrop. A re-escalation of US-China export controls on advanced semiconductors or new energy sanctions would be the key policy actions that would change my views below.

views.note: No new export-control escalation visible in the data, but NVDA's 8-K in June and the still-elevated policy uncertainty index keep me cautious on the structural China-exposure risk.
WTI down 17% over three months to $80 suggests either easing geopolitical supply risk or demand softening; either way the tailwind from energy security premiums is fading.

CAT's Reg FD disclosure in June and the still-above-average policy uncertainty index leave me uncertain on infrastructure/trade-policy direction; a clear fiscal stimulus signal would turn me constructive.

Tight HY spreads at 2.71% and a positively sloped 10y-2y curve at +41bp support bank earnings; multiple recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-markets activity, and no sanctions-related disruption is evident.
No new evidence of supply-chain or China-policy disruption, but the absence of data rather than positive signals keeps conviction low; any new tariff or export-control action would shift me to avoid.
Defensive consumer staples benefit from the still-elevated policy uncertainty backdrop at 284; PG's recent Reg FD filing and stable macro conditions support a modest long.
